entries.name: big O
entries.say: big oh of gee of en
entries.means: an upper bound on growth: the cost grows no faster than g(n), ignoring constant factors, from some input size onward.

entries.name: big theta
entries.say: big thay-ta of gee of en
entries.means: a tight bound: the cost grows exactly like g(n) — bounded above and below by constant multiples of it.

entries.name: big omega
entries.say: big oh-may-ga of gee of en
entries.means: a lower bound on growth: the cost grows at least this fast. How impossibility results are written.

entries.name: little o, little omega
entries.means: the strict versions: grows strictly slower (o) or strictly faster (ω) than g(n) — the bound is not tight.

entries.name: the input size
entries.means: how many items the algorithm is given: elements to sort, keys to store, characters to scan.

entries.name: the cost function
entries.means: the number of steps an algorithm takes on an input of size n; the thing the bounds above describe.

entries.name: logarithm of n
entries.means: how many times n can be halved before reaching 1. In asymptotics the base doesn't matter (it's a constant factor); lg means base 2.

entries.name: floor and ceiling
entries.say: floor of ex, ceiling of ex
entries.means: x rounded down (floor) or up (ceiling) to a whole number — how the analysis stays honest when n doesn't divide evenly.

entries.name: summation
entries.means: add up a sequence of terms — how the cost of a loop is written down before it's simplified.

entries.name: n factorial
entries.means: n × (n−1) × … × 1: the number of orderings of n items, and the growth rate of brute-forcing them.

entries.name: n choose k
entries.means: the number of ways to pick k items from n when order doesn't matter.

entries.name: modulo
entries.means: the remainder after division — the workhorse of hashing and ring buffers.

entries.name: a graph
entries.means: a graph G is a set of vertices V (the dots) and a set of edges E (the connections between them).

entries.name: vertex and edge counts
entries.say: the size of vee, the size of ee
entries.means: how many vertices and edges the graph has — graph algorithms state their cost in both, like Θ(|V| + |E|).

entries.name: degree
entries.means: how many edges touch vertex v. Directed graphs split it into in-degree and out-degree.

entries.name: edge weight
entries.means: the cost, length or capacity of the edge from u to v — whatever the problem is measuring.

entries.name: shortest-path distance
entries.means: the least total weight of any path from s to v — what Dijkstra and friends compute.
